description: §38.1 — the CANONICAL v0.3 channel placement when `<page>` declarations are present: the `<channel>` is a CHILD of `<program>` and a SIBLING of the `<page>` (Insight 30, S87). Channel state stays reachable from inside the `<page>` via canonical `@` access. This is the shape E-CHANNEL-INSIDE-PAGE tells authors to move TO, so it is pinned as an inversion guard: if it ever fires a placement code, the channel-in-page fix has inverted the rule.
rationale: §38.1: "A `.scrml` file's `<program>` element MAY contain zero or more `<channel>` declarations alongside its `<page>` declarations and other body content. Channel state lives at the file scope established by `<program>` and is reachable from inside any `<page>` via canonical `@` access." Neither placement code fires.
